summary: The app has no layout-level shell. `src/app/layout.tsx` is a bare `<html><body>{children}</body></html>` server component with no Sidebar. Instead, EVERY page opts in by wrapping its own JSX in `<AppShell>` (imported as `@/components/AppShell`). `AppShell` is a 58-line client component that renders `<Sidebar />` plus a `<main>` with `marginLeft: SIDEBAR_WIDTH` (260). `Sidebar.tsx` is the single source of truth for left navigation: a module-level `const MENU: MenuSection[]` array of `{ title?, items: MenuItem[] }` sections, where `MenuItem = { href, label, emoji, matchPaths?, children?, dynamicChildren? }`. Icons are literal emoji strings — there is no icon component in the sidebar (antd `@ant-design/icons` is used only inside the `/events` subtree and page bodies, never in the sidebar). There are 4 sections: 콘텐츠 자산, 페이지 · 배너, 이벤트, 도움말. Children are ALWAYS rendered (no expand/collapse state) so a new sub-entry is visible immediately. Active state is computed by `isExactActive(item)` for parents (exact match OR `pathname.startsWith(href + '/')` OR any `matchPaths` prefix OR any child match) and inline for children (hash-aware: `#`-bearing hrefs compare `pathname === base && currentHash === '#'+hash`). One item (`/page-builder`) uses `dynamicChildren: 'pageTemplates'`, which triggers a `fetch('/api/events')` in the Sidebar on every pathname change and renders the last 10 `eventType === 'page'` docs as sub-links. Styling is overwhelmingly inline `const S: Record<string, CSSProperties>` objects declared at the BOTTOM of each file, after the component. Tailwind is in devDependencies but there is NO postcss.config and NO `@import "tailwindcss"` in globals.css — it is dead weight; zero `className=` usage exists in any `src/app/**/page.tsx`. antd is used only in the `/events` subtree (which has its own `src/app/events/layout.tsx` wrapping AntdRegistry + ConfigProvider + App), and that is where the most recent commits landed. No page anywhere reads an `?embed=1` query — `PromptBuilderModal.tsx` sets `embed=1` on its iframe src but `/prompt-builder/page.tsx` ignores it and renders `<AppShell>` unconditionally, so the sidebar currently DOES show inside that modal. The only shell-less page is `/builder`, which simply omits `<AppShell>` entirely (that is the established escape hatch, not a query param).

summary: The 제품등록 subsystem is a 4-file vertical slice: one client page (`src/app/products/page.tsx`, 710 lines), a collection route + an `[id]` route under `src/app/api/products/`, and `src/models/Product.ts`. It is deliberately low-tech: no antd (antd is isolated to the `/events` subtree via `src/app/events/layout.tsx`), no Tailwind classes, no form library, no server components. Everything is a `'use client'` page wrapped in `` with a single trailing `const S: Record = {...}` style dictionary, `useState` per form field (not one form object), and hand-rolled `fetch` calls. DATA FLOW: the page loads via `GET /api/products?category=…&limit=200`, reads `json.ok` then `setItems(json.items)`. Create posts the whole image as a base64 dataURL inside the JSON body of `POST /api/products`; the route itself then relays that base64 to `POST /api/ftp` (server→server, using `req.nextUrl.origin`), which base64-decodes it, streams it over `basic-ftp` to `/web/img/design/` on Cafe24, and returns `{ success:true, imageUrl }`. That https URL is what lands in `productImageUrl`. This is the OPPOSITE of the references page, which uploads multipart from the browser to `/api/ftp` first and then posts only the resulting URL. A third, more robust helper exists (`src/lib/image-upload.ts` → `persistImageToFtp`) with client-side downscaling and a Vercel Blob fallback — the products page does not use it. ENVELOPE: this subsystem (and references/presets/prompt-builder/ai-*) uses `{ ok:true, items|item|count }` / `{ ok:false, message }`. The events/templates/migrate-design routes use a different `{ success:true, data }` envelope, and `/api/ftp` uses `{ success:true, imageUrl }`. New code in the products family must use `ok`. UI SCOPE: list = a CSS-grid card wall (`repeat(auto-fill, minmax(220px,1fr))`) with the image rendered as a `backgroundImage` on a div (not ``, not `SafeImage`). Filters = a single pill row of hardcoded categories that re-fetches server-side. There is NO pagination anywhere (the only pagination in the repo is antd `` at `src/app/events/list/page.tsx:229`), NO search box, and NO edit form — the card only exposes an active toggle (PATCH) and delete (DELETE), even though the PATCH route already whitelists 9 editable fields. AUTH: none. `src/lib/auth.ts` (jose JWT, `admin_session` httpOnly cookie) and `src/models/AdminUser.ts` exist with a seed script, but nothing imports `verifySession()`, there is no `middleware.ts`, and no login page. `/products` and all `/api/products` verbs are fully public.

The products create path pushes the FULL base64 dataURL through JSON: browser → POST /api/products → server → POST /api/ftp. base64 inflates bytes ~33% and Vercel caps serverless request bodies at 4.5MB, so images above roughly 3MB fail with an opaque 413/empty-body error. src/lib/image-upload.ts was written specifically to solve this (shrinkToBudget + multipart + Blob fallback) but products/page.tsx never adopted it. Mirror references/page.tsx (client multipart to /api/ftp) or persistImageToFtp for anything new.

Filename sanitization happens twice and disagrees. src/app/api/products/route.ts:100-101 preserves Hangul (`/[^a-zA-Z0-9가-힣._-]/g`), but src/app/api/ftp/route.ts:15-23 `sanitizeFilename` then strips everything non-ASCII (Cafe24 nginx decodes non-ASCII as EUC-KR and 403s). The DB URL always reflects the FTP-side name, so never predict the stored URL client-side.

Duplicate handling is inconsistent between siblings: POST /api/products returns HTTP 200 with `{ ok:true, item, duplicated:true, message }` on a duplicate `productImageUrl` (route.ts:123-131), while POST /api/references returns HTTP 409 with `{ ok:false }`. Client code that only checks `json.ok` will silently treat a duplicate as a successful create.
DELETE /api/products/[id] is a HARD delete (`findByIdAndDelete`), but DELETE /api/references/[id] is a SOFT delete (`{ active:false }`). Do not copy one's semantics into the other's UI copy.

`productImageUrl` is `unique: true` in the schema, so two products can never share an image URL — re-uploading the same file with a new name works, but re-submitting a known URL silently returns the existing doc.

Product.ts's HMR footer uses the delete-then-`mongoose.model(...)` form with NO `mongoose.models.Product ||` fallback (unlike AdminUser/CampaignTemplate/ReferenceImage which keep the `||` fallback). Copy the Product/BannerPreset variant for a new model in this family or you get an OverwriteModelError inconsistency.

GET /api/products parses `active` as the literal strings 'true'/'false'; any other value (including `active=1`) means no active filter at all, so inactive products leak into a list that forgot the exact string.

The page passes `limit=200` but the route clamps to 500 and defaults to 100 — there is no total count, no cursor, and no pagination UI, so the grid silently truncates past 200 items. `count` in the response is just `items.length`, not a collection total.

The PATCH route accepts category/variant/nameKr/nameEn/thumbnailUrl/visualNotes/tags/recommendedTool/active, but the UI only ever sends `{ active }`. There is no edit form and no /products/[id] page — 'edit' is unimplemented UI, not a missing API.
`productImageUrl` is NOT in the PATCH allowlist, so a product's image can never be replaced after creation — only delete + re-create.

The products grid renders images as `backgroundImage: url(...)` on a div, bypassing SafeImage/proxyImageUrl. That is fine for display but will taint any canvas/html2canvas export; use `<SafeImage>` if the new feature ever rasterizes.

antd is NOT available on /products. `AntdRegistry`/`ConfigProvider`/`<App>` are provided only by src/app/events/layout.tsx, and the root src/app/layout.tsx is bare. Using `AntdApp.useApp()` outside /events will throw.
The `load()` effect has `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` above `}, [filterCategory]);` — the repo tolerates this rather than wrapping loaders in useCallback.
Tailwind is in devDependencies but the products/references pages use zero Tailwind classes; all layout is inline CSSProperties. Don't introduce utility classes here.

`connectToDatabase()` intentionally does not set `dbName` (src/lib/mongodb.ts:24-26) — products/references live in the URI's default DB, while EventPage alone hops to `yogibo` via `useDb()` inside its model.

summary: There is exactly ONE storage that live event pages read from: the Cafe24 web host at `https://yogibo.openhost.cafe24.com/web/img/design/`, written over plain FTP by `POST /api/ftp`. Everything else (Vercel Blob, /api/proxy-image, fal.ai CDN) is either a transient staging hop or an admin-UI-only convenience. FLOW (client → live page): admin builder holds `blob:`/`data:` previews → on save, `uploadBlockImage()` in `src/app/events/create/page.tsx:565` and `src/app/events/edit/[id]/page.tsx:632` calls `persistImageToFtp(blob, filename)` (`src/lib/image-upload.ts:72`) → that client helper shrinks the image (JPEG re-encode + progressive downscale to <2MB, `shrinkToBudget` line 22) and POSTs `multipart/form-data` to `/api/ftp` → the route FTPs the bytes to `/web/img/design/` and returns `{ success:true, imageUrl }` → the returned absolute cafe24 https URL is written verbatim into `EventPage.sections[].src` (Mongo `yogibo` DB, `eventTemple` collection, `src/models/EventPage.ts:99-107`). `POST /api/events` (`src/app/api/events/route.ts:33`) stores `sections` with zero URL rewriting. FLOW (live render): the embed snippet generated in `src/app/events/detail/[id]/page.tsx:292-295` loads `widget.js` from `CAFE24_API_HOST` (the ychat cloudtype deploy, `src/lib/cafe24-api.ts:8-10`) — NOT from this Next app. Inside `public/widget.js`, `renderImageBlock` does `img.src = block.src;` (line 168) with no proxying, no rewriting; popup images (`im.url`, lines 243/273) and event-notice images (line 364) are equally raw. So whatever string is in Mongo is what the browser hits on the cafe24 storefront. Because widget.js is served from the ychat origin (not the Vercel app), a relative `/api/proxy-image?...` URL persisted into a section would 404 in production, and a fal.ai/Vercel-Blob URL would be a foreign, expiring host. Cafe24 URLs work in the live page precisely because a plain `` needs no CORS. /api/proxy-image + proxyImageUrl exist ONLY for the admin app: `yogibo.openhost.cafe24.com` sends no CORS headers, so canvas/`drawImage`/html2canvas/`fetch` from the Vercel admin domain taint or fail. `SafeImage`, `loadSafeImage`, and `MainVisualCanvas` route cafe24 URLs through the same-origin proxy which re-emits `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. The proxy is a closed whitelist of 4 cafe24/yogibo hosts — fal.ai, Vercel Blob, Unsplash are NOT whitelisted and get 403 from it. @vercel/blob is wired but effectively dormant: `/api/upload` only mints a client-upload token and 503s when `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` is missing (it is absent from `.env.local`, which only has MONGODB_URI, FTP_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, FAL_KEY). It is reached only in the extreme branch where an image is still ≥3MB after 11 compression attempts (`src/lib/image-upload.ts:118-132`), and even then the blob is immediately deleted by `/api/ftp` after mirroring to cafe24 (`src/app/api/ftp/route.ts:124-133`). Blob is a payload-size workaround, never a serving host.

gotchas: sanitizeFilename annihilates non-ASCII basenames: `한글배너.png` → base becomes `__` → `_` → stripped to `''` → falls back to `upload_<Date.now()>.png`. The caller cannot predict the URL; it MUST read `imageUrl` from the response. (Rationale in the comment at src/app/api/ftp/route.ts:13-14: cafe24 nginx decodes non-ASCII names as EUC-KR and 403s.)

sanitizeFilename edge case: a name starting with a dot (`.png`) has `lastDot === 0`, so `lastDot > 0` is false and the whole string is treated as the base → result is `png` with NO extension. Cafe24 will serve it without an image content-type.
No collision protection in /api/ftp — an identical sanitized name silently OVERWRITES the existing remote file. Every caller adds `Date.now()` + a random suffix itself.

`ensureDir` was deliberately removed (commit e8d068c 'bypass FTP root permission issue on linux'): cafe24's virtual root returns 550 for cd/mkd from Vercel's Linux runtime. Always upload with the absolute `/web/img/design/<name>` path; never re-add ensureDir/cd.

`persistImageToFtp` short-circuits on any string already matching `/^https?:\/\//` (src/lib/image-upload.ts:77) and returns it UNCHANGED. Passing a fal.ai or Vercel Blob URL to it does NOT copy the file to cafe24 — it silently persists the foreign URL into the event page.
`persistImageToFtp` / `shrinkToBudget` are browser-only (createImageBitmap, document.createElement('canvas')). They cannot be imported from a route handler or server component.

The `{ blobUrl, filename }` branch of /api/ftp fetches ANY publicly reachable URL, not just Vercel Blob (src/app/api/ftp/route.ts:66-78). The subsequent `del(blobUrl)` is wrapped in try/catch and only console.warns, so a non-Blob source URL is harmless — this is the cheapest server-side way to mirror a remote generated image onto cafe24.

Vercel serverless request bodies cap at ~4.5MB. base64 inflates payloads ~33%, which is why the event path uses multipart. The base64 JSON branch (builder/page.tsx:304, prompt-builder/page.tsx:229, products route) is only safe for small images.

The Vercel Blob fallback is effectively dead: `.env.local` has no BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN, so /api/upload returns 503 with a Korean setup message, and any image still ≥3MB after all 11 compression attempts fails to upload entirely.

Size thresholds are inconsistent across copies: src/lib/image-upload.ts uses TARGET_BYTES=2MB / MULTIPART_LIMIT=3MB, while the inlined duplicates in src/app/main-visual/page.tsx:1992 and main-visual-smart-store/page.tsx:1773 still use a 4MB multipart cutoff. Three near-identical implementations exist.

/api/ftp returns HTTP 500 for FTP failures with `{ success:false, message: '<stage> 실패: …', stage }`. `stage` is one of handler-entry|create-ftp-client|parse-body|fetch-blob|ftp-connect|ftp-upload|blob-cleanup — use it when reporting errors.
The FTP client timeout is 30s (FTP_TIMEOUT_MS) inside a 60s maxDuration; a slow cafe24 FTP with a multi-MB file will fail at stage `ftp-upload`.

widget.js runs on the cafe24 storefront domain and is served from the ychat cloudtype origin, so `SELF_BASE` is NOT this Next app. Relative URLs of any kind (including /api/proxy-image) are unresolvable in a published page.

cafe24 returns no CORS headers, so a cafe24 image drawn to canvas in the admin taints it — hence SafeImage/proxyImageUrl. The proxy whitelist is closed (4 hosts, duplicated in two files); fal.ai and blob.vercel-storage.com are rejected with 403 'host not allowed'.

/api/proxy-image buffers the entire upstream response via `arrayBuffer()` before responding, and its 25MB guard only applies when upstream sends `content-length` — a chunked large response bypasses the check.
GET /api/ftp is a live debug endpoint that leaks whether FTP env vars are set plus the raw FTP_HOST/FTP_PORT values, unauthenticated.

The five asset models split into two tiers. **Template-ish models** (`CampaignTemplate`, `MainVisualTemplate`, `CouponTemplate`, `ProductSectionTemplate`) have NO grouping at all — just a business-key string (`templateId`, or `libraryId` for stickers), display fields, and `active: {type: Boolean, default: true, index: true}`; they are served generically by `/api/templates/[type]` through a `getModel(type)` switch and edited as raw JSON in `/admin/templates`. **Gallery-ish models** (`ReferenceImage`, `Product`, `StickerLibraryItem`, `BannerPreset`) add a required, indexed `category`-style enum. `ReferenceImage` is the closest precedent to the new feature and the richest: `category` enum (5 values, indexed, default `web-banner`), optional `platform` enum (8 values + `null`), `tags: [String]`, `visualNotes`, `extractedTokens: Mixed`, `active`, `{ timestamps: true, strict: false }`, plus two explicit compound indexes. `BannerPreset` shows the two-axis variant (`platform` × `device`) with a `{platform:1, device:1, updatedAt:-1}` compound index and the most complete HMR boilerplate. conventions: Model file layout, in order: `import mongoose, { Schema, Document } from 'mongoose';` → a `/** ... ───── */` Korean doc-block explaining the model and every enum value → exported string-literal union types (e.g. `export type ReferenceCategory = 'web-banner' | ...`) → `export interface IX extends Document` with per-field `/** 한국어 설명 */` JSDoc → the Schema → explicit compound indexes → HMR cache invalidation → `export default`.

HMR-safe export — use the NEWER form (BannerPreset/Product/ApiUsage/EventPage), not the legacy `mongoose.models.X || ...` form: delete from `mongoose.models`, try/catch `deleteModel`, then `export default mongoose.model<IX>('X', schema, 'explicit_collection_name');`. Always pass the third collection-name argument (snake_case: `sticker_library`, `banner_presets`, `campaign_templates`, `main_visual_templates`, `products`).

Every library model carries `active: { type: Boolean, default: true, index: true }` and `{ timestamps: true }`. Enum fields that are used for filtering are always `index: true`, and a compound index is added for the real query shape (`ReferenceImageSchema.index({ category: 1, active: 1 })`, `BannerPresetSchema.index({ platform: 1, device: 1, updatedAt: -1 })`).
There is NO `src/models/index.ts` barrel. Import each model directly: `import ReferenceImage from '@/models/ReferenceImage';`. Path alias is `@/* -> ./src/*`.

Route handlers: `export const runtime = 'nodejs';` (and `maxDuration = 300` for bulk/FTP work, `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` on the presets routes). Everything inside one `try { await connectToDatabase(); ... } catch (err: any) { return NextResponse.json({ ok:false, message: err?.message ?? '실패' }, { status: 500 }); }`.

Response envelope for asset APIs is `{ ok: true, items }` / `{ ok: true, item }` / `{ ok: false, message }`. (`/api/templates/*` uses `{ success, data, error }` and `/api/ftp` uses `{ success, imageUrl }` — do NOT mix these into a new asset API; follow `{ ok, items }`.)

Next 16 dynamic params are Promises. Both destructuring styles exist — `ctx: { params: Promise<{ id: string }> }` then `const { id } = await ctx.params;` (references) and `{ params }: { params: Promise<{ id: string }> }` then `const { id } = await params;` (products/presets/templates). Pick one and `await` it.
PATCH always uses an explicit `const allowed = [...]` array and copies only those keys into an `update` object — never spread the request body.

List queries: `const query: any = {}` built imperatively from `searchParams`, `limit` clamped with `Math.min(Number(...) ?? default, hardCap)`, `.sort({ createdAt: -1 })` (or `updatedAt: -1` for presets), `.limit(limit)`, `.lean()`.

Pages are `'use client'`, wrapped in `<AppShell>`, and ALL styling lives in one `const S: Record<string, CSSProperties> = { ... }` object at the bottom of the file. Conditional/active styles are applied by spreading: `style={{ ...S.card, ...(isActive ? S.cardActive : {}) }}`. Do not introduce Tailwind on a gallery page.

Image grids: `{ display:'grid', gridTemplateColumns:'repeat(auto-fill, minmax(200px, 1fr))', gap: 14 }` for browse pages, `minmax(140px,1fr)` for compact pickers; cards are `background:'#fff', border:'1px solid #e5e7eb', borderRadius:10, overflow:'hidden', position:'relative'` with `cardImg: { width:'100%', aspectRatio:'16/10', objectFit:'cover', background:'#f3f4f6' }`.

UI copy, comments, alert()/confirm() text and doc-blocks are in Korean; code identifiers are English. Section headings use circled numerals (`① ② ③`) and emoji prefixes (`📚 레퍼런스 갤러리`, `➕ 새 레퍼런스 추가`, `✕` for delete).

Category option lists in the UI are hard-coded consts shaped `{ value, emoji, label }` (references) or `{ id, emoji, label }` (products), declared above the component, and mapped both into the `<select>` of the create form and the filter chip row.

External images are rendered with `` in gallery cards, but `SafeImage` (`@/components/SafeImage`, auto-proxies cafe24 URLs via `/api/proxy-image` + `crossOrigin="anonymous"`) is the component to use whenever the image may be drawn to a canvas/html2canvas.

Upload flow is always two steps from the client: `FormData` → `POST /api/ftp` → read `json.imageUrl` → `POST` metadata+URL to the resource API. Servers only take base64 and call `/api/ftp` themselves in `POST /api/products`.

## How an event page is built today

`/events/create` and `/events/edit/[id]` are two near-identical ~1,300-line client components ("use client", Ant Design v5 + `@hello-pangea/dnd`). **They are copy-paste twins** — every feature exists twice with slightly different line numbers and small drifts (create has a SHA-256 dedupe on upload, edit does not; edit refuses to delete the last block; create wraps save in `modal.confirm`). Any new UI must be added to BOTH files.

**State shape** is flat and lives entirely in the page component:
- `title: string`, `blocks: EventBlock[]`, `selectedId: string | null`
- `eventCouponNos: string[]`, `pageMaxWidth / pageMaxWidthInput: number | null`
- `allCats: CategoryItem[]`, `couponOptions: CouponOption[]`, `categoryProductsMap: Record<string, ProductLite[]>`
- Region-drawing: `addingMode`, `addType: 'link'|'coupon'|'tab'|'popup'|null`, `pendingRegion`, `dragStartPos`, `dragCurrent`
- Popup editing: `popupImages: PopupImage[]`, `popupShowClose: boolean`
- Notice editing: `noticeImagePreview: string`, `noticeImageFile: File | undefined`
- Five Ant `Form.useForm()` instances: `mapForm`, `editForm`, `videoForm`, `textForm`, `noticeForm`

**Layout** is a two-column flex: left = title / coupon Select / page-max-width / horizontal draggable block strip / a row of "추가" buttons / `<Upload.Dragger>`; right = live preview (`previewScrollRef`, blocks tagged `data-pbid={b.id}`, auto-scrolls to `selectedId`).

**How blocks are added** — every block type follows the same idiom: a modal is opened by `openXModal(blockToEdit: EventBlock | null = null)`; `submitX()` reads `form.getFieldsValue()`, then either patches the selected block or appends a new one with `const id = Date.now().toString() + Math.random()` and calls `setSelectedId(id)`. Image blocks are the exception — they are created directly inside `uploadProps.customRequest` via `FileReader.readAsDataURL`, so an image block starts life as `{ id, type:'image', src: <dataURL>, file, hash, regions: [] }`.

**How images become permanent**: on save, `blocks.map(uploadBlockImage)` walks every block. `uploadBlockImage` (create:565-623, edit:632-688) handles exactly three image slots — `event_notice.noticeImage`, `image.src`, and `regions[].popup.images[].url` — converting `data:`/`blob:` to a permanent cafe24 FTP URL via `persistImageToFtp(blob, filename)` (`src/lib/image-upload.ts`, which JPEG-shrinks >2MB then POSTs multipart to `/api/ftp`). **Anything already matching `/^https?:\/\//` is passed through untouched** — which is exactly why a library picker that hands back an https URL needs zero upload plumbing. Then `file`/`hash` are stripped and the payload `{ title, sections, imageUrl, eventType:'event', couponNos, pageMaxWidth }` is POSTed to `/api/events` (create) or PUT to `/api/events/[id]` (edit). `imageUrl` is derived as `uploadedBlocks.find(b => b.type==='image' && b.src)?.src`.

## Existing image pickers

Three different picker idioms coexist:

1. **`Cafe24ThumbnailPicker`** — a hand-rolled fixed-overlay modal (NOT antd), `z-index: 9999`, closes on backdrop click and ESC. Props `{ open, onClose, onSelect(imageUrl, product) }`. Two-pane flow: product table → click a row → grid of every extractable image → click a tile → `onSelect(img.url, selected)`. It never uploads; it just returns a cafe24 URL string. Renders thumbs through `proxyImageUrl()`.
2. **`ProductBlockModal` / `MorePrd`** — antd `<Modal>`-based, `{ visible, onCancel, onOk(payload) }`. `ProductBlockModal` returns a fully-formed `EventBlock`; `MorePrd` returns `ProductItem[]`. **Neither contains any image URL input** — product imagery comes only from the cafe24 API — so they are *not* integration points.
3. **`PopupImageRegionEditor`** — an inline (non-modal) controlled editor: `{ src, regions, onChange(regions) }`, drag-to-draw ratio regions on an already-chosen image.

The canonical way to make ONE picker serve MANY image slots is the callback-in-state pattern in `PropertiesPanel.tsx:67` — store the setter closure, open the modal when it's non-null, call it on select.

## Where a "라이브러리에서 이미지 가져오기" button belongs

There are exactly **three image-input surfaces per page × 2 pages = 6 sites** (plus 2 dead-link opportunities). All three take a URL string and need no upload path, since `uploadBlockImage` short-circuits on `https://`.

Note: `/page-builder` already links to `/events/create?prefillImage=…` (`src/app/page-builder/page.tsx:118`) with the comment "2단계 라이브러리 연결 자리", but **neither events page reads any search param** — there is no `useSearchParams` anywhere under `src/app/events/`. That link is dead today and is the obvious second hook.

Candidate library data sources that already exist: `GET /api/references?limit=200` (`ReferenceImage`: `{ _id, title, imageUrl, category, platform, tags }`), `GET /api/products` (`Product.productImageUrl`), and `GET /api/events` filtered by `eventType==='banner'|'page'` (`EventPage.imageUrl`) — the latter is how `/banner/cafe24` and `/page-builder` build their galleries.

gotchas: create/page.tsx and edit/[id]/page.tsx are hand-maintained duplicates. Every change must land in BOTH, and they have already drifted: create dedupes uploads by sha256 (`blocks.some(b => b.hash === hash)`, line 149) while edit does not; edit blocks deleting the last block (line 321) while create allows emptying; create wraps save in `modal.confirm` while edit saves directly. Do not assume a line number in one maps to the other.

`EventPage.sections` is `[Schema.Types.Mixed]` with no sub-schema — adding a field to `EventBlock` needs no migration, but Mongoose will also silently persist any junk you leave on the object. That is why `delete rest.file; delete rest.hash;` runs before save (create:649-654, edit:695-700). A transient field added for a library picker (e.g. `libraryItem`) will be persisted unless you strip it there too.

`persistImageToFtp` / `uploadBlockImage` short-circuit on `/^https?:\/\//`, so a library URL is stored verbatim and is NEVER re-hosted. If the library ever serves a non-permanent or non-cafe24 URL (blob store, signed URL, a `/api/...` relative path), the live widget will hot-link it forever and eventually 404. Feed the picker only permanent absolute URLs, or force a re-upload by attaching a `file`.

The create page's sha256 duplicate guard only inspects `b.hash`, which is set only in `customRequest`. Library-sourced blocks have no hash, so the same library image can be added many times with no warning. If dedupe matters, compare `b.src` instead.

summary:
**Bottom line: the AI *image-generation* backend exists and is fully written, but nothing in the app calls it. The only live "AI image" feature is prompt *text* generation that the user pastes into an external tool by hand.**

**1) `/api/generate-image`** talks to **fal.ai over plain `fetch`** — there is no fal SDK in `package.json`, just the synchronous `https://fal.run/...` REST endpoints with an `Authorization: Key ${FAL_KEY}` header. It branches on whether `sourceImageUrl` was supplied:
- absent → `https://fal.run/fal-ai/imagen4/preview/ultra` (Google **Imagen 4 Ultra**, text→image), body `{prompt, num_images, aspect_ratio, negative_prompt}`
- present → `https://fal.run/fal-ai/flux-pro/kontext` (**FLUX Pro Kontext**, image→image edit that preserves the product), body `{prompt, image_url, num_images, guidance_scale: 3.5, safety_tolerance: '2', output_format: 'jpeg'}`

`numImages` is clamped to 1–4. `imageSize` is heavily normalized (`normalizeImageSize` accepts the FLUX enums, `{width,height}`, or a `'1920x680'` string, and downscales past a 14 MP cap) and then `toImagenAspect` collapses it to one of `'1:1'|'16:9'|'9:16'|'4:3'|'3:4'` — **but only the Imagen branch consumes it; the Kontext branch never sends any size at all.** Response is `{ok, model, images: [{url,width,height}], seed, timings, usage}`. The `images[].url` handed back is fal's own CDN URL, verbatim. **Nothing is persisted** — no FTP, no Mongo document, no Vercel Blob. The only write is the usage counter.

Note the file's own header comment is stale: it claims "FLUX 1.1 Pro" for text→image (it's Imagen 4 Ultra now) and the quota key is still named `fal-flux-pro-1.1`.

**2) Quota** is one global Mongo counter, not per-user and not per-month. Both `route.ts:58` and `usage/route.ts:15` hardcode `USAGE_KEY = 'fal-flux-pro-1.1'` (duplicated constant — keep them in sync). `DEFAULT_LIMIT = Number(process.env.FAL_USAGE_LIMIT) || 100` is applied only through `$setOnInsert`, so once the doc exists, changing the env var does nothing. The gate is `if (usage.count + numImages > usage.limit) → 429`; after fal replies, `$inc: {count: generatedCount}` counts *images actually returned*. There is no reservation, so two concurrent requests can both pass the gate. `GET /usage` also returns `estimatedCostUsd = count * 0.04`. `PATCH /usage` accepts `{limit?, reset?}` and has **no auth whatsoever** — anyone can raise the cap or zero the counter. `ApiUsage` lives in collection `apiUsage` on the *default* DB (the URI's `/test`), unlike `EventPage` which is pinned to the `yogibo` DB.

**3) `src/lib/ai-image.ts` does not generate images despite its name.** It is a `'use client'` canvas/color utility module extracted out of `/main-visual`: `sampleEdgeColor`, `runBackgroundRemoval` (dynamic-imports `@imgly/background-removal`, model `isnet_fp16`, `proxyToWorker: false`, returns a `blob:` URL), `extractFirstHex`, `getRelativeLuminance`, `getContrastTextColor`, `isNeutralColor`, `loadImage`. Exactly one consumer: `MainVisualAssistPanel.tsx:11`, which `PropertiesPanel.tsx:1587` renders for `main` sections.

**4) UI callers of `/api/generate-image`: zero.** A repo-wide grep for `generate-image` / `generateImage` / `fal.run` finds only the two route files' own doc comments. `git log` shows the route arrived in the single snapshot commit `e75ddcb` and never acquired a caller. `/api/generate-image/usage` has no admin screen either. What actually ships today is the *prompt* pipeline: `/prompt-builder` (page.tsx:268) POSTs a large form to `/api/prompt-builder`, Claude turns it into a tool-specific English prompt string, the user hits "📋 프롬프트 복사" and "🚀 ChatGPT 새 탭", generates the image in ChatGPT/Midjourney/fal.ai's own web UI, downloads it, and re-uploads it by hand through `FileUploader`/`DragDropUploader`. `PromptBuilderModal` embeds `/prompt-builder` in an iframe and receives the string via `postMessage` `{type:'prompt-builder:result'}`. `products/page.tsx:264` and `PromptBuilderLink.tsx:57` only list "fal.ai" as a *target tool label* for that copy-paste flow.

**5) Both `ai-compose` and `ai-layout` are dead code**, in different ways. `ai-compose` is a working Claude route (`api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`, `CLAUDE_COMPOSE_MODEL` defaulting to `claude-sonnet-4-6`, max_tokens 4000, temp 0.6) that pulls Tier-1 references from `EventPage.find({isReference:true})` and Tier-2 design tokens from `ReferenceImage.extractedTokens`, then returns a synthesized `SectionData` with re-assigned ids. Its only front-end is `src/components/AIComposeForm.tsx` — which **nothing imports** (its own docblock claims `PropertiesPanel.tsx` uses it; PropertiesPanel does not). `ai-layout` is a Gemini 2.5 Flash vision route (retry ladder 0s→1s→2s then `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` fallback) whose sole caller, `handleAIAutoDesignMain`, sits **inside a block comment** in `PropertiesPanel.tsx:269-360` marked "현재 비활성화", with the matching JSX at ~line 859 also commented out. It requires `GEMINI_API_KEY`, which is **not in `.env.local`** (only `MONGODB_URI`, `FTP_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `FAL_KEY`), and `src/lib/ai-vision.ts` documents that the project deliberately migrated off Gemini to Claude Haiku.

**6) Generated images are transient.** The route returns fal's hosted URL and stops. Worse, the repo's persistence helper will not rescue it after the fact: `persistImageToFtp` returns any `https://` string unchanged (`image-upload.ts:77`), so a fal URL dropped into a section's `bgImage`/`src` is skipped at save time and the ephemeral URL is written into Mongo verbatim. Neither `proxy-image`'s `ALLOWED_HOSTS` nor `proxyImageUrl`'s `PROXY_HOSTS` includes `fal.media`, so it isn't CORS-proxied for canvas work either. The only permanent store is cafe24 FTP: blob → `persistImageToFtp` → multipart `POST /api/ftp` → `basic-ftp` upload into `/web/img/design` → `https://yogibo.openhost.cafe24.com/web/img/design/<ascii-sanitized-name>`. To persist server-side, `/api/ftp` already accepts JSON `{blobUrl, filename}` or `{imageBase64, filename}` — that is the natural hook for copying a fal result into permanent storage.

conventions: Every API route opens with a boxed Korean docblock: `/** POST /api/x ───── 입력: {...} 응답: {...} 환경 변수: ... 비용: ... */`. Include a cost estimate when the route hits a paid provider — generate-image, ai-compose, ai-vision and prompt-builder all do.

Route segment config right after imports: `export const runtime = 'nodejs';` plus `export const maxDuration = 60;` (300 for bulk work, `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` for GET/PATCH read routes).

Response envelopes are NOT uniform — match the neighbour you are extending. `/api/generate-image` uses `{ok:false, error}`; `/api/ai-compose`, `/api/ai-layout`, `/api/prompt-builder`, `/api/references/*` use `{ok:false, message}`; `/api/ftp` uses `{success, imageUrl, message}`. New generate-image code must use `error`.

Error handling is always `catch (err: any) { console.error('[route-name] …', err); return NextResponse.json({ ok:false, error: err?.message || 'unknown error' }, { status: 500 }); }` with a bracketed route tag in the log.

Third-party AI providers are called with bare `fetch`, never an SDK. fal.ai: `Authorization: Key ${FAL_KEY}`. Anthropic: `x-api-key` + `anthropic-version: '2023-06-01'`. Gemini: key in the query string.
Missing env var returns a 500 with a Korean instruction naming the variable and `.env.local` (e.g. `'FAL_KEY 환경 변수가 .env.local 에 설정돼 있지 않습니다.'`).
`await connectToDatabase()` from `@/lib/mongodb` before touching any model; the shared connection is globally cached.

Models end with an HMR guard before registering — `if (mongoose.models.X) { mongoose.deleteModel?.('X') }` — and pass an explicit collection name as the third `mongoose.model()` arg (`'apiUsage'`, `'eventTemple'`).

Client components start with `'use client'`, use inline React style objects collected in a bottom-of-file `const S: Record<string, CSSProperties> = { … }`, and use antd only for modals/messages. Tailwind is installed but these components do not use utility classes.
All user-facing strings are Korean with a leading emoji for status (`🪄 AI 분석 중…`, `✅ … 적용 완료`, `❌ …`, `⚠️ …`), and transient statuses are cleared with `setTimeout(() => setStatus(''), 2500-6000)`.
Import paths are mixed — `@/lib/*` and `@/models/*` aliases in routes, relative `'../lib/ai-image'` / `'../app/builder/types'` inside `src/components`. Follow whichever the file already uses.
Numeric user input is clamped defensively at the route boundary (`Math.max(1, Math.min(4, body.numImages ?? 1))`, the `clamp()`/`normalizeHex()` helpers at the bottom of ai-layout).

`DEFAULT_LIMIT` is written with `$setOnInsert`, so `FAL_USAGE_LIMIT` only has effect the very first time the counter document is created. Afterwards the limit can only be changed via `PATCH /api/generate-image/usage`.

`PATCH /api/generate-image/usage` has zero authentication or origin check — any client can raise the limit or reset the counter to 0. There is an `src/lib/auth.ts` and an `AdminUser` model in the repo, but this route does not use them.
The quota check is not atomic: `findOneAndUpdate` with `$setOnInsert` does not reserve capacity, so N concurrent requests can each read the same `count` and all pass the gate before any `$inc` lands.
The counter is a single global lifetime total — no per-user attribution, no monthly rollover, no TTL, no reset job. Someone must PATCH `reset:true` by hand.

`fal.media` is in neither `ALLOWED_HOSTS` (proxy-image/route.ts:29) nor `PROXY_HOSTS` (proxy-image-url.ts:15), so a fal URL is neither proxied nor CORS-safe for `canvas.drawImage` / `getImageData`.

`ai-layout`'s retry loop calls `res.text()` on failures and then, on the non-retryable path, rewraps it in a fresh `Response` because the body was already consumed — the `await geminiRes.text()` at line 212 can still hit an already-read body in some paths. Don't copy that control flow.

FTP filenames are force-sanitized to ASCII (`sanitizeFilename`, ftp/route.ts:15-23) because cafe24's nginx decodes non-ASCII names as EUC-KR and 403s. Any filename you generate should already be ASCII-safe.

`next.config.ts` lists `basic-ftp`, `mongoose`, `mongodb` in `serverExternalPackages` — a route importing a native/socket module must stay `runtime = 'nodejs'` and the package likely needs adding to that list.
